items.scientific_object: Sixteen level-1 QAOA approximation ratios for n=32 random signed 3-regular Ising instances.
items.authored_reason: The independently generated, hash-bound paper-protocol artifact covers this series.  Exact displayed bar identity remains unavailable because the paper does not publish its random graph/coupling samples.

items.scientific_object: Sixteen level-1 RQAOA approximation ratios for n=32 with cutoff n_c=8.
items.authored_reason: The independently generated, hash-bound paper-protocol artifact covers this series.  Exact displayed bar identity remains unavailable because the paper does not publish its random graph/coupling samples.

items.scientific_object: Sixteen level-1 QAOA approximation ratios for n=100 random signed 3-regular Ising instances.
items.authored_reason: The independently generated, hash-bound paper-protocol artifact covers this series.  Exact displayed bar identity remains unavailable because the paper does not publish its random graph/coupling samples.

items.scientific_object: Sixteen level-1 RQAOA approximation ratios for n=100 with cutoff n_c=30.
items.authored_reason: The independently generated, hash-bound paper-protocol artifact covers this series.  Exact displayed bar identity remains unavailable because the paper does not publish its random graph/coupling samples.

items.scientific_object: Degree-3 expander ferromagnetic Ising Hamiltonians obey the symmetry-protected NLTS energy/depth bound, with the proof giving epsilon=h/6 and n>48^2 8^d.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: For an infinite bipartite D-regular family, level-p QAOA has ratio at most 5/6+sqrt(D-1)/(3D) in the stated p-versus-n range.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: A level-p graph-Ising QAOA unitary has two-qubit-gate depth at most p(D+1), tightened to pD for D-regular bipartite graphs.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: QAOA approximation ratios are invariant under the stated boundary-edge sign-flip gauge transformation.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: Every Z2-symmetric range-R circuit on the even ring of disagrees obeys the normalized-energy upper bound (2R+1/2)/(2R+1) for R<n/4.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: The range-R upper bound is exactly tight when n is a multiple of 2R+1 and asymptotically tight up to O(1/n) for fixed R.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: A Z2-symmetric range-p circuit prepares the (2p+1)-qubit GHZ state from |+>.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.source_ref: Lemma B.2 statement and proof, PDF p. 8
items.scientific_object: The printed lemma states <H_n>=(2p+1/2)/(2p+1), while its proof evaluates n times that ratio for the unnormalised H_n.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: The closed-form level-1 QAOA two-spin correlation for a general real symmetric Ising coupling matrix.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.source_ref: Appendix C.4 complexity paragraph, PDF p. 11
items.scientific_object: For n_c=O(1), one correlation costs O(n), one dense RQAOA step O(n^3), and the full level-1 classical simulation O(n^4), independently of variational-circuit depth.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: For the stated 2^(n/3) signed-ring family, a uniform 1-local classical algorithm achieves approximation ratio one.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: For the same signed-ring family, level-p QAOA has approximation ratio at most p/(p+1).
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: For the same signed-ring family, level-1 RQAOA achieves approximation ratio one.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: The printed appendix statement gives <x|H(J)|x>=1 for an unnormalised n-edge Ising Hamiltonian, while the main theorem claims ratio one.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: Level-1 RQAOA returns an exact optimum for every one-dimensional Ising ring with J_k in {+1,-1}.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.source_ref: Lemma D.2 proof endpoint, PDF p. 16
items.scientific_object: The printed proof gives unfrustrated residual/final maxima n_c+1 and n+1 although the Hamiltonians contain n_c and n unit-magnitude terms.
items.authored_reason: No claim-specific independent artifact and fresh falsification result currently close this analytic item.

items.scientific_object: Sixteen level-1 QAOA approximation ratios for n=32 random signed 3-regular Ising instances.
Sixteen level-1 RQAOA approximation ratios for n=32 with cutoff n_c=8.
Sixteen level-1 QAOA approximation ratios for n=100 random signed 3-regular Ising instances.
Sixteen level-1 RQAOA approximation ratios for n=100 with cutoff n_c=30.
Degree-3 expander ferromagnetic Ising Hamiltonians obey the symmetry-protected NLTS energy/depth bound, with the proof giving epsilon=h/6 and n>48^2 8^d.
For an infinite bipartite D-regular family, level-p QAOA has ratio at most 5/6+sqrt(D-1)/(3D) in the stated p-versus-n range.
A level-p graph-Ising QAOA unitary has two-qubit-gate depth at most p(D+1), tightened to pD for D-regular bipartite graphs.
QAOA approximation ratios are invariant under the stated boundary-edge sign-flip gauge transformation.
Every Z2-symmetric range-R circuit on the even ring of disagrees obeys the normalized-energy upper bound (2R+1/2)/(2R+1) for R<n/4.
The range-R upper bound is exactly tight when n is a multiple of 2R+1 and asymptotically tight up to O(1/n) for fixed R.
A Z2-symmetric range-p circuit prepares the (2p+1)-qubit GHZ state from |+>.

items.source_ref: Lemma B.2 statement and proof, PDF p. 8
items.scientific_object: The printed lemma states <H_n>=(2p+1/2)/(2p+1), while its proof evaluates n times that ratio for the unnormalised H_n.
The closed-form level-1 QAOA two-spin correlation for a general real symmetric Ising coupling matrix.

items.source_ref: Appendix C.4 complexity paragraph, PDF p. 11
items.scientific_object: For n_c=O(1), one correlation costs O(n), one dense RQAOA step O(n^3), and the full level-1 classical simulation O(n^4), independently of variational-circuit depth.
For the stated 2^(n/3) signed-ring family, a uniform 1-local classical algorithm achieves approximation ratio one.
For the same signed-ring family, level-p QAOA has approximation ratio at most p/(p+1).
For the same signed-ring family, level-1 RQAOA achieves approximation ratio one.
The printed appendix statement gives <x|H(J)|x>=1 for an unnormalised n-edge Ising Hamiltonian, while the main theorem claims ratio one.
Level-1 RQAOA returns an exact optimum for every one-dimensional Ising ring with J_k in {+1,-1}.
